title: The Sigil of the Glass Steppe
premise: Petra Voss, a royal food-taster whose palate is secretly a form of the forbidden gift—reading memory and intent through taste—keeps double ledgers for the Glasswrights' Guild, which trades in bottled memories and impossible bargains. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps the capital, Petra discovers the queen herself is dying of a stolen memory that could reignite the ancient war between the gift-bearers and the throne, and that his own guildmaster sold her the poison. To save the queen and expose the guild, Petra must drink the stolen memory himself, risking the erasure of his own identity; in the end he returns what was taken at the cost of forgetting who he loved, choosing duty over self while planting the seed of a new accord between crown and gifted.
about_author: Felix Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers from vanished trading houses before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burning fantasy about ordinary people trapped inside systems of power.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At a royal banquet, Petra tastes a dish laced with something no poison ledger can name—a ghost of someone else's grief—and quietly logs it. We learn his double life: taster by day, keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers by night. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Ledgers Written in Salt
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the guild vault, Petra records a trade: a widow sells her wedding day for bread money. His guildmaster, Corvane, notices him lingering over the entry and warns him that curiosity is a debt. Beat: unease—the first hint the guild trades in more than memories.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Criers announce the Gift-Hunt: anyone bearing the old blood must register or burn. Petra watches a neighbor dragged away and realizes his tasting-gift makes him prey. He burns one page of the guild ledger to protect himself. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Queen Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Summoned to taste for the queen privately, he detects a foreign memory lodged in her like a splinter—she is fading, forgetting her own reign. She mistakes him for her long-dead brother. Beat: pity entangled with terror as he realizes the palace itself is compromised.

chapters.title: The Glasswright's Price
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Corvane reveals the guild bottled the queen's stolen memory years ago and sold it—to an anonymous buyer within the court. He orders Petra to find the buyer using his gift, or be reported to the Hunt. Beat: betrayal; the guild was never neutral.

chapters.title: A Cup of Someone Else
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Following the memory's flavor through the palace kitchens, Petra identifies its signature on the cup of Lord Chancellor Aldery—but the trail splits: two cups, two buyers. Introduce Sefa, a sharp-eyed undercook who notices him noticing. Beat: first alliance, tentative warmth.

chapters.title: The Second Buyer
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Through her eyes we see Petra as dangerous and magnetic; she admits she has been copying palace accounts for someone she won't name. Their clues interlock: a faction wants the queen's war-memory released to justify purging all the gifted. Beat: reluctant trust.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Register
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The Hunt reaches the guild's street; a bottler Petra knows is burned alive rather than register. Corvane's response is cold bookkeeping. Petra realizes Corvane engineered the purge to corner the memory market. Beat: grief curdling into hatred.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Steppe
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Corvane takes Petra to the guild's true vault beneath the glass flats outside the city, where the queen's stolen memory sits in a vial that hums like a struck bell. Touching it, Petra glimpses the ancient war's final night. Beat: awe and dread; the stakes become mythic.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa's mysterious employer is revealed: Aldery, who offers her immunity in exchange for testifying that Petra is gifted. She stalls, torn between survival and the man she's begun to trust. Beat: temptation and guilt.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Aldery hosts a dinner where every course is a trap—dishes brewed to force confessions from gifted palates. Petra survives by performing ignorance, but leaves knowing Aldery holds enough evidence to hang him. Beat: claustrophobic tension, near-exposure.

chapters.title: The Taste of Home
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Hiding in Sefa's rooms, Petra tastes a simple stew and is flooded by his own buried childhood—his mother was a memory-worker burned in the last purge. He confesses everything to Sefa. Beat: vulnerability; love declared in the shadow of the Hunt.

chapters.title: Corvane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Confronted, Corvane lays out his logic: the gifted will only survive as assets, not people, and the queen's war-memory is leverage to buy their place. He offers Petra partnership. Beat: seductive corruption—power offered as mercy.

chapters.title: The Queen's Brother
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The queen, lucid for one hour, tells Petra the truth: she stole her own war-memory to stop herself from unleashing the old weapons, and it is killing her. She asks him to destroy it, not return it. Beat: moral crisis—two queens' wishes, one vial.

chapters.title: Sefa's Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Cornered by Aldery, Sefa gives false testimony—not against Petra but against Aldery's faction, burning her own safety. She flees to Petra with the copied accounts proving the plot. Beat: sacrifice; the alliance becomes love made public and punishable.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Hunted by both crown and guild, the pair cross the glass steppe to the vault, pursued by Corvane's collectors. A running battle on the mirror-flats; Sefa is wounded shielding Petra. Beat: desperate momentum, cost made flesh.

chapters.title: The Vial and the Knife
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the vault, Corvane corners them: drink the memory and wield the war, or die. Petra pretends to accept, then shatters the containment rig—but the memory, freed, pours toward the nearest vessel: him. Beat: climax begins; choice collapses into instinct.

chapters.title: The War Inside
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Inside the stolen memory, Petra relives the ancient war's end and the queen's original sin, holding the memory's fury together by will alone while his own past begins dissolving to make room. Beat: interior climax—identity versus duty fought sip by sip.

chapters.title: What Petra Voss Chose
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. From outside, Sefa watches Petra carry the memory back to the palace and pour it past the queen's lips, naming each piece as it returns so she can refuse the war. The queen wakes whole; Aldery's faction falls. Beat: triumph shadowed by visible loss.

chapters.title: The Empty Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra stands trial-adjacent as the queen grants the gifted registration instead of fire, using his testimony and the ledgers as proof of the guild's crimes. Corvane escapes into the steppe, unpunished. Beat: justice incomplete; victory with a scar.

chapters.title: A Stranger at My Own Table
chapters.summary: POV Petra. The price comes due: Petra cannot remember Sefa—only that he once loved someone. She stays anyway, teaching him their story one meal at a time, tasting as remembrance. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; love rebuilt from notes.

chapters.title: The Sigil of the Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: POV Petra. On the salt flats, Petra burns the guild's ledgers and carves a new sigil—a cup and an open hand—for the accord between crown and gifted. Somewhere beyond the horizon, Corvane is already trading again. Beat: resolution with a door left open; memory, like power, always finds new vessels.
